column3: A circular emblem: an elegant laurel wreath enclosing a single bunch of grapes with two vine leaves, centered, symmetrical, like a seal on a classic French wine label. Centered on the canvas with generous margins, the emblem fills about 60% of the width.

A refined monogram: a single classical serif capital letter L intertwined with a fine vine tendril and one laurel sprig, centered, like a crest on a classic French wine label. The letter L is the only character. Centered with generous margins, the emblem fills about 55% of the width.

A minimal emblem: two laurel branches curving upward and meeting to form the silhouette of a wine tasting glass, with one small grape cluster at the base. Centered, symmetrical, generous margins, the emblem fills about 50% of the width.

A medal emblem: a round competition medal hanging from a short folded ribbon, the medal face engraved with a bunch of grapes framed by laurel leaves, like an award seal on a classic French wine label. Centered with generous margins, the emblem fills about 55% of the width.

A wide panoramic landscape of rolling vineyard hills in France, neat vine rows following the slopes, a small stone village with a church steeple, and a winding country road crossing the vineyards toward distant mountains, like the view of a road trip through wine country.

An antique engraved map of France's wine regions seen from above, with delicate hatched vineyard areas, rivers, small ornamental compass rose and decorative cartouche frames, and a dotted travel route crossing the country from north to the Alps. Absolutely no lettering or place names anywhere on the map.

A long country road running straight through vineyard rows in perspective toward low hills at golden hour, a single small vintage car on the road, cypress and plane trees along the way, calm and inviting.

A decorative horizontal frieze along the bottom third of the canvas: a long vine branch with leaves, tendrils and two grape clusters entwined with laurel sprigs, running edge to edge, like the ornamental border of a classic French wine label.
A crossroads in the middle of vineyards with an old wooden signpost whose arms carry no writing, a winding road disappearing between vine rows toward a hilltop village.

A tasting table at a wine competition: three tasting glasses, a judging notebook with a pen, and three competition medals with ribbons laid on the tablecloth, seen from a slight overhead angle. No bottles.
